summary: A proposal that the Network Information Center collect and keep answers to questions about what programs and services are available on the ARPANET, prompted by a MITRE request for information about resources of certain types. The idea became the Resource Notebook. It is a suggestion, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC proposes that the Network Information Center collect answers about programs available on the network. It also asks whether the ARPANET should focus on research or serve outside information needs.

subtitle: A proposal for the NIC to collect information about network programs.

tldr.problem: Researchers had asked where to find types of programs available on the network, including macro processors and data management systems.
tldr.mechanism: L. Peter Deutsch proposes that the Network Information Center keep the replies in a repository that could include programs and documentation.
tldr.outcome: The RFC raises the proposal and broader questions about the network community's role; it does not report a decision to implement it.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 446's status as Unknown. The RFC is a proposal and a discussion of the network's role.

sections.title: A Place to Find Network Programs
sections.content:
Requests for information about network resources, including macro processors, data management systems, and electromagnetic wave analysis programs, prompted this proposal. L. Peter Deutsch suggests that the Network Information Center (NIC) collect the replies.

The document proposes organizing knowledge and techniques, as well as programs, so that the network community can find them.
sections.plainLanguage: Researchers were asking which programs were available on the network. The proposal asks the NIC to collect and organize the answers.

sections.title: Extending the NIC's Catalog
sections.content:
The NIC already had catalog and keyword facilities for the Journal and an index of computer-related documents that were not online. Deutsch argues that the system could be extended to cover programs and documentation.

He expects such an extension would not require major effort and could help research sites find resources, but frames this as a proposal.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC already cataloged documents. Deutsch suggests adding information about programs and their documentation.

sections.title: Research Network or Information Service
sections.content:
The RFC raises a wider question about the network community's obligations to outside users, including government agencies. It contrasts that role with the ARPANET's stated function as a network research experiment and with research in computing more broadly.

Deutsch says the network's status as both a service network and a research effort creates confusion and frustration. The note invites consideration of that tension.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks whether the ARPANET should mainly support research or also provide information services to outside organizations. He says the community has not adequately considered this tension.
